en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Cittalatā Grove in the Itthivimāna (The Female Vimānas)
6. The Story of the Mansion of Soṇadinnā “O goddess,
with such exquisite beauty with which you stand there— ”
Illuminating all directions like a star among the herbs,
by what means do you possess such a complexion?
By what means do you succeed here?
Whatever riches arise that are dear to the mind, they come to you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your radiance illuminates all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she gave an answer regarding the fruit of that karma:
"They knew me as Soṇadinnā."
In Nāḷandā there was a female lay follower,
endowed with faith and virtue,
who always delighted in sharing.
I gave clothing, food, lodgings, and lamps to those who were upright.
With a serene mind,
on the fourteenth and the fifteenth,
and on the eighth day of the lunar fortnight.
And during the fortnight of miracles,
I shall observe the Uposatha day, perfectly endowed with its eight factors.
Always restrained in our virtue,
self-controlled and generous,
we dwell in this celestial mansion.
Abstaining from taking life,
restrained from false speech,
and from theft and sexual misconduct,
And far removed from the drinking of intoxicants,
they delight in the five precepts and are skilled in the Noble Truths.
I am a female lay follower of Gotama, the illustrious one who possesses vision;
by that [merit], my complexion is such as this.
And my radiance shines in all directions.
Thus ends the sixth Vimāna, the Soṇadinnā-vimāna.
